destinations.name: Cairo & Giza
destinations.tagline: Cradle of Antiquity, Pyramids & Grand Metropolises
destinations.shortDescription: Marvel at the Great Pyramids of Giza, the Sphinx, and the treasures of King Tutankhamun inside the world-class Grand Egyptian Museum.
destinations.description: A vibrant tapestry where five millennia of world history seamlessly converge with dynamic modern elegance. From the monumental Giza Plateau guarding the Great Pyramids and the Sphinx to the newly unveiled Grand Egyptian Museum, Cairo offers unscripted wonder at every turn. Wander through the medieval minarets of Islamic Cairo, browse spice-laden alleys in Khan El Khalili bazaar, and savor refined gastronomy overlooking the Nile.
highlights: Private VIP Access to the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM)
Sunset Camel & Horseback Safari across Giza Plateau
Curated Islamic & Coptic Cairo Heritage Alleys
Exclusive Dinner Cruising along the Nile River

practicalInfo.bestSeason: October to April (Mild, sunny daytime & crisp desert evenings)
practicalInfo.climate: Arid desert climate with comfortable winter temperatures (18°C - 25°C)
localTips: Book Grand Egyptian Museum VIP permits in advance for private hall entry.
Early morning visits to the Pyramids avoid both crowds and midday heat.
Private chauffeur service is essential for seamless metropolis navigation.

destinations.name: Luxor
destinations.tagline: The World’s Greatest Open-Air Archaeological Museum
destinations.shortDescription: Unveil the Valley of the Kings, the monumental Karnak Temple, and Queen Hatshepsut’s terraced sanctuary on the West Bank.
destinations.description: Built on the ancient capital of Thebes, Luxor holds an unmatched concentration of monumental architecture. Sail the peaceful Nile to the West Bank to enter subterranean royal tombs adorned with vibrant 3,000-year-old hieroglyphic frescoes in the Valley of the Kings. Gaze in awe at the colossal Hypostyle Hall of Karnak Temple and soar silently in a sunrise hot air balloon over Hatshepsut’s mortuary monument.
highlights: Exclusive Private Opening of Queen Nefertari’s Tomb
Sunrise Hot Air Balloon Flight over Ancient Thebes
Torchlight Night Tour of Illuminated Luxor Temple
Avenue of Sphinxes Walk connecting Karnak to Luxor

practicalInfo.bestSeason: November to March (Pleasantly warm days, cool starry nights)
localTips: Visit the Valley of the Kings early at 06:00 AM for undisturbed stillness.
Don’t miss Nefertari’s tomb (QV66) in the Valley of the Queens.
Take a private sunset felucca ride around Banana Island.

destinations.name: Aswan
destinations.tagline: Timeless Nile Tranquility & Rich Nubian Soul
destinations.shortDescription: Discover the romantic island temple of Philae, emerald granite cataracts, and colorful Nubian traditions on the shores of Lake Nasser.
destinations.description: Egypt’s sunniest southern outpost where the Nile flows at its most poetic, weaving past massive pink granite boulders and emerald islands. Aswan invites unhurried contemplation. Explore the sacred island sanctuary of Goddess Isis at Philae Temple, sip afternoon high tea on the historic terrace of the Sofitel Legend Old Cataract, and sail by private felucca into authentic painted Nubian settlements.
highlights: Boat Crossing to the Sacred Island Temple of Philae
High Tea on the Historic Old Cataract Terrace where Agatha Christie wrote
Private Felucca Cruise around Elephantine Island & Botanical Gardens
Nubian Village Cultural Immersion & Artisanal Spice Markets

localTips: Sunset views from the Old Cataract terrace are unparalleled.
Combine Aswan with an early morning excursion to Abu Simbel.
Purchase authentic hibiscus flowers and Nile spices in the local souk.

destinations.name: Abu Simbel
destinations.tagline: Monumental Colossi of Ramesses II on Lake Nasser
destinations.shortDescription: Witness the four colossal seated statues of Ramesses II carved into the cliff face, rescued from the rising waters of Lake Nasser.
destinations.description: Rising majestically from the tranquil desert waters of southern Lake Nasser, Abu Simbel stands as the supreme testament to pharaonic ambition and modern UNESCO engineering. Carved into a sandstone mountain in the 13th century BC, the twin temples honor Ramesses the Great and his beloved Queen Nefertari, aligned with mathematical precision to illuminate the inner sanctuary during the Sun Festival.
highlights: Twin Mountain-Carved Temples of Ramesses II and Queen Nefertari
Biannual Solar Alignment Phenomenon in the Inner Sanctum
UNESCO Architectural Miracle: Relocation of the Entire Mountain
Desert Flight or Private Lake Nasser Expedition Cruise Arrival
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: October to March (Special Sun Festival in Oct & Feb)

practicalInfo.airport: Abu Simbel Airport (ABS) with daily flights from Aswan/Cairo
practicalInfo.recommendedStay: 1 Day or Overnight for Sound & Light Show
localTips: Fly in on the early morning flight or stay overnight to witness sunrise before day-tripper coaches arrive.
Don’t miss the subtle love poetry inscribed inside Nefertari’s temple.

destinations.name: Alexandria
destinations.tagline: Pearl of the Mediterranean & Greco-Roman Legacy
destinations.shortDescription: Walk the legendary Corniche, explore the Bibliotheca Alexandrina, and uncover Roman catacombs beneath the Mediterranean waves.
destinations.description: Founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BC, Alexandria balances Mediterranean charm with profound classical legacy. Fanned by sea breezes along its sweeping seaside Corniche, Alexandria reveals subterranean treasures like the Catacombs of Kom El Shoqafa, the historic Citadel of Qaitbay overlooking the ancient Pharos Lighthouse site, and the striking contemporary Bibliotheca Alexandrina.
highlights: Bibliotheca Alexandrina: World-Famous Modern Revival of the Ancient Library
Subterranean Catacombs of Kom El Shoqafa Roman Burial Galleries
Citadel of Qaitbay Standing on the Site of the Ancient Pharos Lighthouse
Fresh Mediterranean Seafood Dining on the Waterfront Corniche

practicalInfo.bestSeason: Spring through Autumn (Moderate Mediterranean sea breezes)
practicalInfo.climate: Mediterranean coastal climate; mild winters and refreshing coastal summers
practicalInfo.airport: Borg El Arab Airport (HBE) or 2.5 hrs luxury transfer from Cairo
localTips: Pair your visit with an authentic Greek-Alexandrian seafood lunch.
A stroll down the historic Corniche at sunset captures the city’s nostalgic elegance.

destinations.name: Hurghada
destinations.tagline: Red Sea Riviera, Pristine Reefs & Luxury Resorts
destinations.shortDescription: Dive into turquoise waters, lounge on private coral sandbanks, and experience world-class all-inclusive coastal hospitality.
destinations.description: Stretching along the azure coast of the Red Sea, Hurghada is Egypt’s premier beach haven for travelers seeking sublime relaxation, vibrant coral reefs, and year-round sunshine. From private yacht charters to Giftun Island to desert quad biking across rolling Eastern Desert dunes, Hurghada pairs effortless leisure with thrilling outdoor escapades.
highlights: Private Yacht Excursion to Giftun Island and Orange Bay
Scuba Diving & Snorkeling in World-Renowned Coral Gardens
Sunset Quad Biking & Bedouin Dinner in the Eastern Desert
Luxury Waterfront Promenade at Hurghada Marina
destinations.bestTimeToVisit: All Year Round (Prime in Autumn & Spring)

practicalInfo.bestSeason: Year-round sunshine; March–May and Sept–Nov offer ideal waters
practicalInfo.climate: Subtropical marine desert; dry warm weather
localTips: Take a private catamaran to secluded reef drop-offs away from the crowds.
El Gouna, just 25 minutes north, offers high-end lagoons, golf, and dining.

destinations.name: Sharm El Sheikh
destinations.tagline: Sinai’s Crown Jewel & World-Class Diving Capital
destinations.shortDescription: Explore the marine biodiversity of Ras Mohammed National Park, luxurious cliffside resorts, and vibrant Sinai nightlife.
destinations.description: Perched on the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula between the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba, Sharm El Sheikh is celebrated globally for its pristine marine reserves. Ras Mohammed National Park boasts towering coral walls dropping thousands of feet into crystal waters teeming with tropical marine life, while luxury 5-star resorts offer cliffside infinity pools and fine dining.
highlights: Ras Mohammed National Park World-Class Marine Sanctuary
Straits of Tiran Scuba Diving & Dolphin Sightings
Exclusive Sunset Yacht Cruises with Gourmet Seafood
Gateway to Mount Sinai and St. Catherine Monastery Excursions

practicalInfo.climate: Arid coastal desert with warm sea temperatures
localTips: Dive Shark and Yolanda Reefs for peak marine biodiversity.
Consider an overnight extension to climb Mount Sinai for sunrise.

destinations.name: Dahab
destinations.tagline: Bohemian Coastal Haven, Blue Hole & Windsurfing
destinations.shortDescription: Relax in relaxed seafront cafes, snorkel the world-famous Blue Hole, and trek the majestic canyons of the Sinai desert.
destinations.description: With its bohemian soul, golden sand beaches, and rugged mountain backdrop, Dahab provides a tranquil, laid-back antidote to bustling resort cities. Renowned worldwide for the underwater abyss of the Blue Hole and the sheltered lagoon of Blue Lagoon, Dahab draws free-divers, kitesurfers, and wellness seekers looking for authenticity and natural peace.
highlights: Snorkeling & Freediving the World-Famous Blue Hole
Boat or Camel Safari to the Remote Ras Abu Galum Nature Reserve
Kite-surfing and Wind-surfing in Dahab Lagoon
Seaside Bedouin Lounges with Fresh Juices and Shisha

practicalInfo.climate: Sunny desert seaside with consistent coastal breezes
practicalInfo.airport: Sharm El Sheikh (SSH) + 1 hr private scenic mountain transfer
localTips: Stay in an eco-boutique hotel along the Lighthouse reef.
Experience dinner under the stars at Wadi Qnai Bedouin camp.

destinations.name: Marsa Alam
destinations.tagline: Pristine Southern Reefs, Dugongs & Sea Turtles
destinations.shortDescription: Swim alongside gentle sea turtles and wild dugongs in Abu Dabbab Bay, surrounded by intact virgin coral atolls.
destinations.description: Egypt’s southern frontier on the Red Sea remains an untouched paradise for marine enthusiasts and discerning eco-travelers. Here, crystal turquoise lagoons host resident green sea turtles, rare dugongs (sea cows), and spinning dolphins at Sataya Reef. Far removed from commercial crowds, Marsa Alam offers peaceful eco-luxury resorts nestled between golden desert and crystal sea.
highlights: Swim with Wild Dugongs and Giant Sea Turtles at Abu Dabbab
Sataya Reef (Dolphin House) Snorkeling Expedition
Elphinstone Reef Diving for Advanced Divers & Oceanic Whitetips
Wadi El Gemal National Park Desert & Mangrove Safari

practicalInfo.bestSeason: Autumn and Spring for crystal underwater visibility
localTips: Visit Abu Dabbab Bay early in the morning for calm waters and active feeding turtles.
Wadi El Gemal is a sanctuary for migratory birds and ancient Roman emerald mines.

destinations.name: Siwa Oasis
destinations.tagline: Mystic Desert Sanctuary, Salt Lakes & Alexander’s Oracle
destinations.shortDescription: Float weightlessly in hyper-saline turquoise pools, explore the mud-brick fortress of Shali, and consult the Oracle of Amun.
destinations.description: Deep in the Western Desert near the Libyan border, Siwa Oasis is an enchanting world unto itself. Famous for its mud-brick fortress of Shali, hundreds of thermal freshwater springs, crystalline turquoise salt lakes where you float effortlessly, and the historic Temple of the Oracle where Alexander the Great was confirmed as the son of Amun.
highlights: Floating in Surreal High-Salinity Turquoise Salt Pools
Sunset at the 13th-Century Mud-Brick Citadel of Shali
Temple of the Oracle of Amun visited by Alexander the Great
Great Sand Sea 4x4 Dune Bashing & Desert Camping

practicalInfo.bestSeason: October to April (Warm pleasant days, cool desert nights)
practicalInfo.currency: EGP cash preferred in oasis markets
practicalInfo.airport: Private charter flight or scenic overland private vehicle from Cairo / Alexandria
localTips: Stay at an authentic Kershef eco-lodge built from local clay and salt rock.
Bathe in Cleopatra’s Spring and sample fresh Siwan dates and olive oil.

destinations.name: White Desert
destinations.shortDescription: Camp under billions of stars amidst chalk monoliths shaped like mushrooms, eagles, and surreal towers by desert winds.
destinations.description: A landscape of hypnotic alien beauty in the heart of Egypt’s Western Desert. Millions of years of wind and sand erosion have carved blindingly white calcium-chalk formations into surreal sculptures that resemble colossal mushrooms, sphinxes, and icebergs rising out of golden dunes. An overnight Bedouin camp here under the pristine Milky Way is a transformative travel experience.
highlights: Glamping under the Starlit Sky at the White Desert National Park
Surreal Chalk Formations: The Mushroom, Chicken & Giant Sphinx
Crystal Mountain Sparkle and Agabat Valley Panoramic Dunes
Authentic Campfire Dinner prepared fresh by Bedouin Guides

practicalInfo.climate: Desert extremes: warm sunny days, chilly star-filled nights
practicalInfo.airport: Accessible by 4x4 expedition vehicle via Bahariya Oasis from Cairo
localTips: Pack warm thermal layers for nighttime desert stargazing.
High-clearance 4WD vehicles and licensed desert navigators are mandatory.

destinations.name: Black Desert
destinations.tagline: Volcanic Basalt Cones & Martian Desert Vistas
destinations.shortDescription: Witness dramatic volcanic peaks capped in black dolerite rock contrasting vividly against the golden desert floor.
destinations.description: Formed by ancient volcanic activity millions of years ago, the Black Desert presents an extraordinary geological contrast to the neighboring White Desert. Black dolerite-capped cones rise out of the ochre sands, creating a cinematic, almost Martian panorama. Climbing the English Mountain offers breathtaking 360-degree views across the surreal volcanic valley.
highlights: Climb English Mountain for Epic 360° Volcanic Valley Vistas
Stark Visual Contrast between Dark Basalt Cones and Golden Sands
Ancient Prehistoric Iron & Volcanic Formations
Seamless Connection on the Safari Trail to Bahariya & White Desert

practicalInfo.airport: Overland expedition from Cairo via Bahariya Oasis
practicalInfo.recommendedStay: 1 Day (often paired with White Desert overnight)
localTips: Wear sturdy footwear with grip if you plan to climb the volcanic mounds.
Combine with the nearby hot mineral springs of Bahariya Oasis.

destinations.name: Fayoum Oasis
destinations.tagline: Wadi El Hitan Whales, Magic Lake & Pottery Villages
destinations.shortDescription: Explore the UNESCO fossil valley of prehistoric whales, sandboard giant dunes into Magic Lake, and visit Tunis pottery village.
destinations.description: Located just 90 minutes southwest of Cairo, Fayoum Oasis is an oasis of prehistoric wonders, tranquil lakes, and artistic heritage. Wadi El Hitan (Valley of the Whales), a UNESCO World Heritage site, displays intact 40-million-year-old walking whale skeletons embedded in desert sandstone. Nearby, Tunis Village charms with artisanal terracotta ceramics, boutique eco-lodges, and views over Lake Qarun.
highlights: Wadi El Hitan UNESCO Prehistoric Whale Skeleton Valley
Sandboarding and 4x4 Dune Adventures at Magic Lake
Artisanal Pottery Workshops in Bohemian Tunis Village
Waterfalls of Wadi El Rayan & Bird Watching at Lake Qarun

practicalInfo.climate: Pleasant oasis microclimate with fresh lake breezes
practicalInfo.airport: 1.5 hrs private chauffeur transfer from Cairo
localTips: Tunis Village is the premier destination in Egypt for bespoke pottery.
Plan sunset at Magic Lake to watch the water shift colors against the dunes.

destinations.name: Edfu
destinations.tagline: The Monumental Temple of the Falcon God Horus
destinations.shortDescription: Step through the towering pylon of Egypt’s best-preserved Ptolemaic temple dedicated to Horus the Falcon.
destinations.description: Positioned midway between Luxor and Aswan along the banks of the Nile, Edfu is home to the Temple of Horus—universally recognized as the most completely preserved ancient temple in Egypt. Shielded by desert sand for two millennia, its mammoth 36-meter-high entrance pylon, intact roofed hypostyle chambers, and sacred golden barque chamber reveal ancient temple liturgy in vivid detail.
highlights: Colossal Black Granite Falcon Statues Guarding the Main Portal
Inscriptions of the Sacred Drama: Mythological Battle of Horus & Seth
Intact Roofed Hypostyle Halls and Royal Sacrificial Chambers
Classic Horse Carriage Ride through the Riverside Town

practicalInfo.bestSeason: October to April (Standard port of call on Nile Cruises)
practicalInfo.airport: Luxor (LXR) or Aswan (ASW) + Nile Cruise or private vehicle transfer
localTips: Arrive at dawn with your cruise Egyptologist before mid-day heat and large tour parties.
Inspect the walls of the outer corridor for the fascinating Nilometer records.

destinations.name: Kom Ombo
destinations.tagline: Dual Sanctuary of Sobek the Crocodile & Horus the Falcon
destinations.shortDescription: Perched on a dramatic bend of the Nile, this unique symmetrical temple honors two rival gods and houses mummified crocodiles.
destinations.description: Dramatically perched on a picturesque promontory overlooking a sweeping bend of the Nile, Kom Ombo is unique in Egyptian architecture. The complex is completely symmetrical, with twin entrances, twin sanctuaries, and paired halls honoring two opposing deities: Sobek the crocodile god of fertility and Horus the Elder the winged falcon god. The site includes ancient medical instrument reliefs and an adjacent Crocodile Mummy Museum.
highlights: Unique Symmetrical Dual Temple Dedicated to Sobek & Horus
Ancient Carved Surgical & Medical Instruments Reliefs
Crocodile Mummy Museum displaying Intact Ancient Reptilian Relics
Spectacular Sunset Moorings directly at the Temple Steps

localTips: Visiting at twilight when the sandstone is lit up against the Nile is unforgettable.
Examine the ancient calendar carvings near the rear sanctuary.

destinations.name: Saint Catherine
destinations.tagline: Mount Sinai Sunrise Trek & Sacred Burning Bush Sanctuary
destinations.shortDescription: Ascend the biblical Mount Sinai for sunrise and visit the world’s oldest continuously inhabited Christian monastery.
destinations.description: Nestled in a remote granite canyon at the foot of Mount Sinai (Jabal Musa), Saint Catherine’s Monastery is a UNESCO World Heritage sanctuary of profound spiritual and historical importance. Founded by Emperor Justinian in the 6th century, it protects the Living Burning Bush, priceless early Christian icons, and one of the world’s oldest libraries. The night trek up Mount Sinai rewards travelers with a sunrise across jagged red peaks.
highlights: Overnight Ascent of Mount Sinai for a Radiant Desert Sunrise
St. Catherine Monastery: The Oldest Continually Inhabited Monastery
The Sacred Relic of the Living Burning Bush
UNESCO-Listed Collection of 6th-Century Encaustic Icons & Manuscripts

practicalInfo.bestSeason: September to November and March to May
practicalInfo.climate: Alpine high-elevation desert: warm days, freezing mountain nights in winter
practicalInfo.airport: Transfers from Sharm El Sheikh (2.5 hrs) or Dahab (1.5 hrs)
localTips: Dress in warm windproof layers for the summit sunrise.
Local Bedouin guides accompany every mountain trek for safety.

destinations.name: Wadi El Natrun
destinations.tagline: Cradle of Christian Monasticism in the Western Desert
destinations.shortDescription: Visit the four fortified 4th-century Coptic desert monasteries that preserved monastic scholarship across the millennia.
destinations.description: Located in a natural depression northwest of Cairo along the desert highway to Alexandria, Wadi El Natrun is the historic birthplace of Christian monastic asceticism. Since the 4th century AD, holy hermits and scholars have sought solitude here. Today, four majestic fortified desert monasteries—Deir Anba Bishoy, Deir al-Suryan, Deir al-Baramus, and Deir Abu Maqar—still practice continuous prayer, surrounded by lush date palms.
highlights: Fortified 4th-Century Coptic Monasteries in the Desert
Historic Wall Frescoes & Ancient Syriac Christian Manuscripts
Peaceful Contemplation and Meeting Resident Monks
Ancient Natron Salt Lakes used in Pharaonic Mummification

practicalInfo.airport: 1 hr luxury private vehicle transfer from Cairo or Alexandria
localTips: Modest dress covering shoulders and knees is strictly required inside the monasteries.
A wonderful cultural stopover when traveling between Cairo and Alexandria.

destinations.name: Nuweiba
destinations.tagline: Sinai Eco-Lodges, Colored Canyon & Gulf of Aqaba Serenity
destinations.shortDescription: Unwind in beachfront bamboo huts, trek through the kaleidoscopic Colored Canyon, and gaze across the Gulf of Aqaba.
destinations.description: Nuweiba is the peaceful soul of the Sinai coast. Situated between the red-hued granite mountains of the Sinai and the serene blue waters of the Gulf of Aqaba, Nuweiba is legendary for simple eco-chic bamboo camps where the sand meets the sea. Nearby, the famous Colored Canyon presents a hiker’s paradise of winding sandstone narrows glowing with violet, copper, and magenta ribbons.
highlights: Hiking the Prismatic Rock Formations of the Colored Canyon
Beachfront Bamboo Hut Eco-Resorts right on the Coral Sand
Gazing Across the Gulf of Aqaba toward the Mountains of Jordan & Saudi Arabia
Quiet Coral Reef Snorkeling with Zero Boat Crowds

practicalInfo.climate: Warm coastal breezes and sunny skies
practicalInfo.airport: Taba Airport or transfer from Sharm El Sheikh / Dahab
localTips: Hike the Colored Canyon with an experienced local Bedouin guide.
Ideal retreat for digital detox, yoga, and contemplative coastal relaxation.

destinations.name: Ain Sokhna
destinations.tagline: Warm Gulf Waters & Mount Galala Coastal Luxury
destinations.shortDescription: Egypt’s closest Red Sea beach to Cairo, featuring warm mineral springs, upscale resorts, and Mount Galala cable car.
destinations.description: Meaning "The Hot Spring" after the thermal sulfuric springs bubbling nearby at Mount Ataka, Ain Sokhna is Cairo’s premier coastal retreat, situated just an hour’s drive from the capital on the Gulf of Suez. With calm swimmable waters year-round, dolphin-watching boat trips, and the state-of-the-art Galala resort city and cable car perched 700 meters above sea level, it provides the ultimate seaside getaway.
highlights: Fast 1-Hour Private Highway Connection from Cairo
Galala Mountain Cable Car with Panoramic Red Sea Views
Private Yacht Charters for Deep-Sea Fishing and Dolphin Watching
Thermal Sulfur Springs and Mountain Spas

practicalInfo.bestSeason: Year-round; spring and autumn are perfection
practicalInfo.climate: Warm sunny maritime climate with tranquil gulf waters
practicalInfo.airport: 1 hr private transfer from Cairo International Airport (CAI)
localTips: Perfect coastal weekend addition before or after a cultural Cairo itinerary.
Visit the historic St. Anthony and St. Paul monasteries located in the nearby Galala mountains.

tours.title: Giza Pyramids, Sphinx & Grand Egyptian Museum VIP Tour
tours.subheadline: Exclusive Egyptologist-led access to the Seven Wonders & Tutankhamun’s treasures
tours.overview: Experience the iconic Giza Plateau and the legendary Grand Egyptian Museum in unparalleled comfort. Stand before the Great Pyramid of Khufu, uncover the enigmatic Great Sphinx, and explore King Tutankhamun’s complete tomb collection with your private accredited Egyptologist.
tours.description: Begin your journey with private chauffeur pick-up from your Cairo or Giza hotel in a climate-controlled luxury vehicle. Arrive at the Giza Plateau before the mid-day heat. Your personal Egyptologist will unravel the engineering genius and cosmological secrets behind Khufu, Khafre, and Menkaure. Enjoy an optional panoramic camel ride with the trio of pyramids rising on the horizon. Afterward, savor an authentic Egyptian gourmet lunch overlooking the plateau. In the afternoon, proceed with skip-the-line VIP entry to the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) to behold Tutankhamun’s gilded chariots, royal thrones, and golden death mask.
highlights: Private accredited Egyptologist guide throughout the day
Skip-the-line VIP entrance to the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM)
Up-close access to the Great Sphinx and Valley Temple of Khafre
Gourmet lunch with sweeping views of the Giza Plateau
Door-to-door private Mercedes or luxury van transfers
included: Private licensed Egyptologist guide
All monument and museum entry tickets with VIP lane access
Chauffeured luxury air-conditioned transport
Gourmet lunch at 9 Pyramids Lounge or Mena House
Bottled mineral water, cold Egyptian hibiscus, and towels
excluded: Entry inside the burial chamber of the Great Pyramid (optional add-on)
Personal gratuities / tipping for guide and driver
inclusions: Private licensed Egyptologist guide
All monument and museum entry tickets with VIP lane access
Chauffeured luxury air-conditioned transport
Gourmet lunch at 9 Pyramids Lounge or Mena House

itinerary.title: Morning: Giza Plateau & Great Sphinx
itinerary.desc: Depart hotel at 08:30 AM. Arrive at the plateau for an in-depth private tour of Khufu and Khafre, followed by the Valley Temple and Sphinx enclosure.

itinerary.title: Midday: Egyptian Gourmet Lunch
itinerary.desc: Savor traditional grilled meats, fresh mezze, and Egyptian dips with uninterrupted panoramic vistas of the nine pyramids.

itinerary.title: Afternoon: The Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM)
itinerary.desc: Step into the colossal atrium beneath Ramesses the Great colossus. Tour the Grand Staircase and Tutankhamun’s complete 5,000-piece royal treasure galleries.

tours.inquiryInfo: Available daily with flexible morning start times. Special private sunrise openings can be arranged upon request.

tours.title: The Royal Pyramid Evolution: Saqqara, Dahshur & Memphis
tours.subheadline: Walk inside the Bent and Red Pyramids and explore Djoser’s Step Pyramid complex
tours.overview: Before Giza existed, pharaonic master builders perfected the art of pyramid construction at Saqqara and Dahshur. This connoisseur tour takes you deep inside the tranquil royal necropolises of the Old Kingdom.
tours.description: Travel south of Cairo through peaceful date palm groves to Saqqara, where architect Imhotep constructed the world’s first stone monument: the Step Pyramid of King Djoser. Venture inside the subterranean tomb of Mehu and the Pyramid of Unas, adorned with the earliest known Pyramid Texts. Continue to Dahshur to descend inside Pharaoh Sneferu’s Red Pyramid and marvel at the angle-shifting Bent Pyramid, concluding with Memphis, the ancient pharaonic capital.
highlights: Explore Djoser’s Step Pyramid Complex & Imhotep Museum
Descend directly inside the burial chamber of the Red Pyramid
Marvel at the mysterious architectural angle of the Bent Pyramid
View the colossal fallen statue of Ramesses II at ancient Memphis
included: Private accredited Egyptologist guide
All entrance fees to Saqqara, Dahshur, and Memphis
Interior entry to the Red Pyramid and Pyramid of Unas
Air-conditioned private vehicle and hotel transfers
Farm-to-table countryside lunch

itinerary.title: Saqqara Necropolis & Step Pyramid
itinerary.desc: Explore Djoser’s limestone enclosure, the Serapeum bull vaults, and high-relief Noble Mastaba tombs.

itinerary.title: Dahshur Royal Pyramids
itinerary.desc: Climb inside the peaceful Red Pyramid and inspect the unique casing of the Bent Pyramid.

itinerary.title: Open-Air Museum of Memphis
itinerary.desc: Visit the first capital of unified Egypt and gaze upon the 10-meter limestone colossus of Ramesses II.

tours.title: Historic Cairo, Saladin Citadel & Khan El Khalili Walking Tour
tours.subheadline: Medieval minarets, Mamluk palaces, and bustling artisanal alleyways
tours.overview: Discover why medieval Cairo was crowned the "City of a Thousand Minarets". Trace centuries of Islamic architecture from the hilltop Citadel down to the vibrant brass and spice quarters of Khan El Khalili.
tours.description: Ascend to the 12th-century Citadel of Saladin, offering commanding vistas over Cairo’s skyline. Step inside the soaring domes of the Great Mosque of Muhammad Ali, lined with alabaster stone. Stroll down historic Al-Mu’izz Street, the greatest concentration of medieval Islamic architecture in the world, and conclude with mint tea and pastries at the historic El Fishawy Cafe in Khan El Khalili bazaar.
highlights: Citadel of Saladin and the magnificent Alabaster Mosque
Walking tour of Al-Mu’izz Street (UNESCO World Heritage)
Sultan Hassan & Al-Rifa’i monumental mosque architecture
Mint tea and aromatic shisha stop at historic El Fishawy Cafe
included: Private expert cultural guide
All entry tickets to Citadel, Alabaster Mosque, and historic complexes
Private air-conditioned transfers
Traditional tea and sweets at El Fishawy

itinerary.title: Saladin Citadel & Muhammad Ali Mosque
itinerary.desc: Tour the fortress ramparts and grand Ottoman-style alabaster dome.

itinerary.title: Al-Mu’izz Street & Khan El Khalili Souks
itinerary.desc: Stroll past Mamluk madrasas, gates, and browse copper craft workshops.

tours.title: Full-Day Luxor Masterpiece: Valley of the Kings, Karnak & Hatshepsut
tours.subheadline: The complete Theban royal journey covering both banks of the Nile
tours.overview: Experience the crown jewels of ancient Thebes in one seamless, private day. Enter subterranean royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings and stand amidst the 134 towering columns of Karnak.
tours.description: Cross the Nile in the gentle morning light to explore the West Bank. Walk deep into three royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings with your Egyptologist, admiring murals that look freshly painted after 3,000 years. Marvel at the dramatic colonnaded terraces of Queen Hatshepsut’s Temple set against towering limestone cliffs, and pause before the massive Colossi of Memnon. After a leisurely lunch, explore Karnak’s Hypostyle Hall and the grand Luxor Temple.
highlights: 3 royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings (Tutankhamun permit available)
Queen Hatshepsut’s Mortuary Temple at Deir el-Bahari
Colossal Hypostyle Hall at Karnak Temple
Luxor Temple connected via the newly restored Avenue of Sphinxes
included: Private licensed Egyptologist guide
All monument entrance fees
Private luxury air-conditioned vehicle throughout the day
Nile-side gourmet lunch
Cold bottled water and refreshments
excluded: King Tutankhamun & Seti I special tomb tickets (available as add-ons)

itinerary.title: Morning: West Bank Royal Necropolis
itinerary.desc: Explore the Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut Temple, and Colossi of Memnon.

itinerary.title: Midday: Riverside Lunch
itinerary.desc: Relax at a traditional riverside restaurant on the Nile bank.

itinerary.title: Afternoon: East Bank Temples

tours.title: Abu Simbel Sun Temples: Private Day Expedition

articles.title: The Ultimate Guide to the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM)
articles.excerpt: Step inside the largest archaeological museum in the world, home to the complete treasures of King Tutankhamun and thousands of royal artifacts.
articles.author: Resident Egyptology Directorate
content: Situated at the foot of the Giza Plateau, the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) represents the crowning architectural and archaeological milestone of 21st-century Egypt.

Spanning over 500,000 square meters, the sanctuary houses over 100,000 antiquities, including—for the first time in human history—the complete, intact collection of King Tutankhamun’s 5,398 funerary treasures in one unified hall.

Upon entering the museum’s immense glass-walled atrium, visitors are greeted by the colossal 3,200-year-old pink granite statue of Pharaoh Ramesses II, suspended effortlessly within soaring architectural lines that frame the Great Pyramids outside through colossal panoramic windows.
Ascending the monumental Grand Staircase, chronologically curated artifacts narrate the evolution of kingship, royal mortuary rituals, and divinity through the Old, Middle, and New Kingdoms.

Our VIP private tours offer priority early access, private Egyptologist curatorial walk-throughs, and exclusive access to the conservation laboratories where pharaonic gold and cedar barques are preserved.

articles.title: Why a Private Dahabiya Is the Purest Way to Sail the Nile
articles.excerpt: Discover why twin-masted sailing vessels offer an intimate, wind-driven voyage impossible to match on larger commercial cruise liners.
articles.author: Captain Tarek & Flotilla Curators
content: Before diesel engines and multi-deck river cruisers navigated the Nile, 19th-century royalty, aristocrats, and early scholars journeyed along the eternal river aboard Dahabiyas: graceful twin-masted sailing yachts propelled purely by the northerly desert wind.

Unlike massive commercial liners carrying hundreds of passengers, a private Dahabiya accommodates just 8 to 12 guests. It can moor at serene river islands, Nubian village coves, and secluded monuments such as Gebel el-Silsila that large cruisers cannot access.
With no engine roar or exhaust vibration, the only sounds are the billow of white canvas, the lapping of the Nile against teak hull timbers, and the song of kingfishers among the papyrus reeds.
Dining on teak decks under the star-drenched Egyptian night sky, accompanied by an onboard private chef and personal Egyptologist, transforms the river journey into pure poetry.

articles.title: Beyond Tutankhamun: Secret Tombs of Luxor’s West Bank
articles.excerpt: Explore the vivid astronomical ceilings of Seti I and the subterranean masterpieces tucked away in the Valley of the Nobles.
articles.author: Antiquities Field Researchers
content: While the world marvels at Tutankhamun’s golden treasures, seasoned scholars know that the finest ancient Egyptian royal wall reliefs lie elsewhere in the Theban Necropolis.

Tomb KV17—the subterranean sepulcher of Pharaoh Seti I—stretches more than 137 meters into the limestone mountain. Its subterranean astronomical ceilings, rendered in vivid lapis lazuli and gold leaf pigments, remain as vibrant today as when royal painters sealed them 3,300 years ago.

Equally mesmerizing is Tomb QV66 in the Valley of the Queens: the eternal resting place of Queen Nefertari, known as "The Sistine Chapel of Ancient Egypt" for its masterfully shaded bas-reliefs illustrating her journey through the Duat underworld.
On our bespoke Luxor journeys, guests enjoy private opening permits to Seti I, Nefertari’s tomb, and the intimate aristocratic tombs of Sennefer and Rekhmire in the Valley of the Nobles.
